reason: Complete HTML full text incl. appendices A-H (comparison, datasets, human audit, Algorithm 1, schema, error taxonomy, analyses, case studies) read; no page images. In scope through the Error Book (validator-driven constraint accumulation injected into later compilation prompts) and the retained Wiki; the retrieval agent itself is not self-modifying.

paper.title: Retrieval as Reasoning: Self-Evolving Agent-Native Retrieval via LLM-Wiki
paper.central_claim: Compiling documents into interlinked Wiki pages, letting an agent traverse them with search/read tools, and maintaining the Wiki with a persistent Error Book (detect -> attribute -> constraint -> inject -> verify/close, plus two-layer code/LLM repair) beats flat and graph RAG on HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA (2.0-8.1 F1 over the strongest baseline) and gives the best overall accuracy on AuthTrace; each of Wiki structure, progressive traversal and Error Book contributes.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker by claude-kimi; model type configured by controller (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: LLM-compiled knowledge bases can introduce dangling links, index inconsistencies, unsupported facts, and cross-page contradictions, yet existing pipelines lack a persistent loop for detecting, repairing, and reducing the recurrence of such errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap relevant to self-evolution: construction errors recur and are not fed back into the compilation procedure.

evidence.quote: Third, it supports self-evolution through an Error Book that records systematic compilation errors, attributes root causes, converts them into reusable constraints, and drives both deterministic code fixes and periodic LLM-based repair.
evidence.support_explanation: Statement of the self-evolving component.

evidence.quote: At index time, LLM-Wiki compiles each source batch against the current Wiki state.
evidence.support_explanation: Incremental compilation loop: select pages, generate updates, validate, update Error Book.

evidence.quote: The Error Book improves the Wiki over time by injecting learned constraints into future compilation prompts and repairing existing errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Two coupled effects are bundled in the Error Book: prompt-constraint learning (non-weight improver state) and direct repair of existing pages.

evidence.quote: After each compilation batch, deterministic validators detect structural errors, while source-grounded LLM verification and cross-page consistency checks identify content-level errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal: deterministic validators for structure, LLM verification (same model family) for content; no QA-answer feedback.

evidence.quote: All open constraint rules are appended to the Step 2 compilation prompt, guiding the LLM to avoid known error patterns in subsequent batches.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistence and later use: all open natural-language constraints are appended to the compile prompt; no cap, merge or conflict handling is described.

evidence.locator: Sec 3.3 Self-Correction Loop, Verify and Close
evidence.quote: Periodically, the system re-validates previously erroneous pages. If the error no longer appears after constraint injection, the error entry is marked as closed.
evidence.support_explanation: Closure criterion is re-validation of the originally erroneous pages; it does not test whether a constraint harms other pages or other error types.

evidence.quote: Layer 1 keeps the Wiki structurally valid, while Layer 2 improves factual grounding and cross-page consistency.
evidence.support_explanation: Layer 1 (deterministic auto-fix of dangling links, formats, index) and Layer 2 (LLM periodic fix every N articles) are static repair, not learned.

evidence.quote: Dangling links account for 29.1–63.8% of detected errors across corpora, and malformed references account for 18.9–28.5%
evidence.support_explanation: On the three public corpora dangling links + malformed references are roughly 78-86% of detected errors (Table 7), i.e., mostly mechanically checkable structure errors that Layer 1 code fixes anyway.

evidence.quote: The source corpus for each benchmark is the union of the context paragraphs associated with those 500 examples, and the same corpus is used for all methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation is on the first 500 questions of each dataset with corpora built from those questions' own context paragraphs (small closed corpora, e.g., 3,440 passages for 2Wiki); no open-domain retrieval and no dev/test split.

evidence.quote: we also use GLM-5.1 for those steps, so that differences primarily reflect retrieval and knowledge organization strategies rather than model choice
evidence.support_explanation: Same LLM for compile, baselines' indexing and answering; baselines run with authors' official implementations and recommended hyperparameters.

evidence.quote: LLM-Wiki uses a larger query-time tool-call budget, but we report latency in Table
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede unequal query-time budgets (up to 15 tool calls vs single-shot top-5 baselines); baselines are not given an iterative/agentic budget.

evidence.quote: on MuSiQue, LLM-Wiki outperforms Dense RAG by 12.9 F1 points and the strongest baseline, LightRAG, by 8.1 F1 points
evidence.support_explanation: Headline gains; HotpotQA gain over LightRAG is 2.0 F1 on 500 questions, single run.

evidence.quote: On Single-doc questions, HippoRAG 2 outperforms LLM-Wiki by 2.3 AC points.
evidence.support_explanation: The best-overall claim on AuthTrace is driven by multi-doc columns; single-doc is lost to HippoRAG 2.

evidence.quote: This variant removes the compiled Wiki representation and uses flat source chunks as the retrieval substrate while retaining the same agent framework and answer generation model.
evidence.support_explanation: Good control: same agent and tool loop over flat chunks; F1 drops 6.1-7.0 points, so structure rather than agentic multi-round access explains a large part of the gain.

evidence.quote: This variant uses the same Wiki compilation and traversal pipeline but disables Error Book updates, constraint injection, and repair.
evidence.support_explanation: The ablation removes learning (constraints) and deterministic/LLM repair together; the 3.4-4.0 F1 drop cannot be attributed to the self-evolving constraint accumulation specifically.

evidence.quote: The 3.4–4.0 F1-point drop suggests that the Error Book improves downstream retrieval by reducing the impact of recurring structural and semantic construction errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Interpretation offered without a measurement of error recurrence rates with and without constraint injection.

evidence.quote: Three authors independently annotate each response using the same 0–3 answer-correctness rubric as the GPT-4o-mini judge.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge validity audit on 240 stratified responses (3 methods) with 89.6% agreement and kappa 0.79; annotators are the authors, blind to method identity.

evidence.locator: Appendix G Generalization Across Answer LLMs
evidence.quote: we evaluate GPT-4o as an alternative answer LLM while keeping the compiled Wiki fixed
evidence.support_explanation: Only the query-time answer LLM is varied; compile LLM and Error Book are not varied (GLM-5.1 throughout).

evidence.quote: making initial construction more expensive than chunk-and-embed approaches, though the cost is amortized over later queries
evidence.support_explanation: Compile-time cost is acknowledged but not quantified for LLM-Wiki, the Error Book overhead, or the graph baselines.

evidence.quote: as the Wiki grows to tens of thousands of pages, directory indices may become unwieldy and page selection may degrade
evidence.support_explanation: Scale boundary: largest evaluated Wiki is ~5.8k knowledge pages (2Wiki); stale-fact handling and web-scale maintenance are future work.

evidence.quote: 2–4 hops requiring an average of 8.2 traversal steps
evidence.support_explanation: Query-time cost is reported per method (s/q) and pages read per query; useful but covers inference only.

evidence.quote: These methods operate within a single inference episode or at query time, whereas the Error Book targets persistent cross-batch error patterns in knowledge construction through constraint accumulation and repair.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors position the Error Book against single-episode self-correction (Reflexion, Self-Refine, Self-RAG); agent-memory systems with persistent curation are not discussed as neighbors.

evidence.quote: Overall, LLM-Wiki preserves performance on simpler 2-hop settings while its advantage increases with reasoning depth and compositionality.
evidence.support_explanation: Gap grows with hop count; supported by hop-wise and type-wise tables (e.g., 2Wiki 4-hop gap to LightRAG 8.3 F1).

signatures.object: Wiki knowledge base (Markdown pages with metadata, aliases, tags, bidirectional wikilinks, directory indices, source archives) compiled by an LLM from raw documents
signatures.information: For each source passage: selected existing pages (SelectPages, k<=5), directory indices, active Error Book constraints; GLM-5.1 as compiler
signatures.operation: CompileWikiPages generates page/link/index updates; validators check structure and content; code auto-fix after every batch; LLM periodic fix every N articles; three-round code-fix <-> LLM-fix loop at finalization
signatures.output: Updated Wiki; traversable by wiki_search / wiki_read
signatures.conditions: Closed corpora of 3.4k-ish passages (2Wiki) to 5.8k pages; same corpus for all methods
signatures.selection_rule: Validator pass/fail and repair; no measured utility gate
signatures.persistence: File tree of pages plus provenance digests
signatures.later_use: Agent traversal at query time (T_max=15, patience 3); later compilation batches select pages from the evolving Wiki
signatures.claimed_effect: Large gains over flat RAG, up to +16.9 F1 over Dense RAG under GPT-4o on 2Wiki
signatures.failure_boundary: Scale (tens of thousands of pages), stale facts, compile cost

signatures.object: Error Book (error_book.yaml): entries with error phenomenon, root cause, constraint rule, verification method and open/closed status; constraints are appended to the compile prompt
signatures.information: Validator-detected errors per batch; LLM attributes root causes and writes natural-language constraints
signatures.operation: Discover -> attribute -> constrain -> inject -> verify and close (every 10 batches)
signatures.output: Open constraint set injected into subsequent compilation prompts; closed entries drop out
signatures.conditions: Errors must be detectable by validators; no outcome-of-QA feedback
signatures.selection_rule: A constraint is created for each attributed error pattern; closed when re-validation of the originally erroneous pages no longer shows the error; no regression test
signatures.later_use: Compile prompt of every later batch
signatures.claimed_effect: Removing Error Book (constraints and repair) costs 3.4-4.0 F1
signatures.failure_boundary: No bound on constraint count, no conflict or retirement logic described; recurrence reduction not measured

signatures.object: Query-time agent policy (search-first / browse-first traversal with sufficiency check)
signatures.information: wiki_search (names/aliases/tags before content) and wiki_read (indices or pages with links); at least one read before answering
signatures.operation: Compose tool calls until all reasoning chains are traced, budget T_max=15, or 3 consecutive empty searches
signatures.conditions: Static harness; not self-modified by task outcomes
signatures.failure_boundary: Single-doc detail loss relative to HippoRAG 2

gap.author_gap: Flat-chunk RAG exposes retrieval as lookup; structured KBs compiled by LLMs degrade (dangling links, unsupported facts, contradictions) without a persistent self-correction loop.
gap.checked_gap: The retrieval-organization gap is concrete and supported by structure ablations. The self-evolution gap (errors recur across batches and need accumulated constraints) is asserted; recurrence is not measured, and the data show most detected errors are mechanically fixable link/format errors.
gap.lineage: RAG -> hierarchical/graph RAG (RAPTOR, GraphRAG, HippoRAG 2, LightRAG) -> 'LLM Wiki' pattern (Karpathy) -> compiled Wiki + Error Book.
gap.closest_adjacent: HippoRAG 2, LightRAG, GraphRAG, RAPTOR (baselines); Self-RAG/Reflexion (query-time self-correction). Persistent LLM-curated agent memories (A-Mem, Mem0-style editors) and iterative RAG (IRCoT) are not compared; adjacency to those is therefore unestablished.
gap.residue: Construction-error recurrence and whether constraint learning (vs deterministic repair) matters; scale; stale-fact handling.
gap.stakes: Reliability of LLM-compiled knowledge used by multi-hop reasoning agents.
gap.method_response: Compile to linked pages, agent-planned traversal, validator-driven Error Book with two-layer repair.
gap.remaining_gap: Scaling beyond ~6k pages, dynamic corpora, measured self-evolution benefit, cross-corpus transfer of constraints.
unresolved: Is the Error Book gain due to learned constraints or to repair?

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C25: the learned model emits a structured, machine-checkable artifact (schema-conforming Wiki pages with links and source references) and the loop is closed by validators during construction (dangling-link, index-consistency, regex reference checks; LLM verification for content) with deterministic auto-fix; the responsibility boundary between LLM (content) and code (structure) is explicit in the two-layer repair. Missing: ablating the verifier to show collapse to baseline (Error Book ablation bundles constraints and repair), cost accounting of the delegated checks, prompts disclosure.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: typed externally verifiable artifact at the handoff - met for structure, weaker for content (LLM verifier); feedback from obtainable signals - met. Failure: 'no ablation isolates the mechanism' partly applies to the Error Book; 'cost unmeasured' applies to compile-time cost.
matches.reason: The index-time pipeline decomposes compilation into LLM generation vs deterministic validation/repair via a schema-typed artifact; the query-time agent is a separate static traversal harness.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest original card is decompose_and_delegate (C25); fit is partial because the paper's headline idea (compile knowledge into navigable structure) is a knowledge-organization choice rather than a solver hand-off.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: structure ablation supports the organization claim; the persistent self-correction problem (recurrence) is not shown to be resolved.

matches.condition_checks: Structure certified by ablation against flat retrieval over the same material (met: same agent on flat chunks); content/index decoupled (directory indices and aliases vs pages; met); local incremental updates per batch (partial; per-passage LLM compile with cost unmeasured); maintenance off the critical path (index-time, met). The stored items are compiled documents rather than agent experience, so fit to the 'experience' framing is only medium.

The Error Book turns observed errors into rule-like lessons (root cause + trigger-like constraint) written to a persistent store injected into later compilation: S3 grounding signal met (validators); S4 maintenance partial (open/closed only, no merge/forget/cap); S5 gate on what is kept unmet (no measured utility); F5 (no outcome-grounded store) avoided. Lessons are about the compiler's mistakes, not task episodes.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS 'close the loop with a verifier's output during construction' = H00 'ground lessons in an observed outcome signal'; here the verdicts come from code/LLM validators and become compile-prompt constraints.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS card delegates to a sound external solver; H00 expects task-outcome reflection. Content-level checks use the same LLM family, weakening soundness.

expectations.applies_when: Lessons are written to a store
expectations.reason: Deterministic validators and source-grounded checks decide which errors become constraints; this is not self-assessment prompting.
Open/closed lifecycle with periodic re-validation; no consolidation, merging, forgetting threshold or cap on the number of constraints appended to every compile prompt.

expectations.applies_when: A gate decides what is kept
expectations.reason: Constraints are admitted when attributed and are closed when the original error disappears; no test that a constraint helps or avoids harming other pages.

expectations.applies_when: No outcome-grounded store (status met = failure avoided)
expectations.reason: The store is grounded in validator-observed compilation errors.
Flat-chunk variant with the same agent and answer LLM isolates the Wiki substrate; w/o traversal and w/o Error Book are also reported (single run).
Incremental compile against the current Wiki state with page selection and deferred LLM repair, but per-passage LLM compile cost is unquantified.

expectations.applies_when: Store built from the test stream (status partial = failure partly present)
expectations.reason: The Wiki is compiled from the context paragraphs of the same 500 evaluation questions, as for all baselines; no QA labels or answers feed the Error Book, but there is no separate construction/evaluation stream.

expectations.applies_when: Model outputs enter memory without external gate (status met = avoided)
expectations.reason: Compiled pages pass deterministic structural validators, but content gating relies on LLM verification from the same model family.
Query latency per method and pages read are reported; index-time cost and Error Book overhead are not quantified.
Three leave-one-out ablations; the Error Book ablation bundles constraint learning and repair, and the validator itself is not ablated.
Compile, attribution and agent prompts are not given in the material searched (only schema, algorithm and examples).
Three QA datasets plus AuthTrace and a second answer LLM; all are closed small corpora with GLM-5.1 compiling.
Seven baselines run with official implementations, but none is an iterative/agentic RAG (IRCoT, Self-RAG) with a matched multi-round budget; query-time budgets differ.
No measurement of error recurrence or error counts with vs without constraint injection, and no repair-only control separating learning from deterministic repair.
No seeds, intervals or tests; the HotpotQA margin over LightRAG is 2.0 F1.

claims.text: LLM-Wiki beats RAG, graph RAG and hierarchical RAG baselines on HotpotQA, MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA by 2.0-8.1 F1 over the strongest baseline.
claims.setting: First 500 questions per dataset; corpus = union of their context paragraphs; GLM-5.1 for all LLM steps
claims.baseline_control: closed-book, BM25 RAG, dense RAG, RAPTOR, GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG 2
claims.selection_vs_test: no dev/test split; no tuning described
claims.counterevidence: Unequal query-time budgets; no agentic RAG baseline; HotpotQA margin small.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On these small closed corpora the compiled-Wiki agent has the highest point F1/EM, with the largest margins on multi-hop compositional questions.

claims.text: Wiki structure, progressive traversal and Error Book each contribute (6.1-7.0, 11.7-13.8 and 3.4-4.0 F1).
claims.baseline_control: flat chunks with same agent; single search+read; no Error Book
claims.counterevidence: Error Book ablation also removes deterministic repair; no variance.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Structure and traversal contributions are well supported; the Error Book contributes through an undifferentiated bundle of constraints and repair.

claims.text: The Error Book mitigates recurring construction errors via constraint accumulation.
claims.counterevidence: No recurrence-rate measurement; most errors are mechanical link/format errors.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Error Book plus repair improves final QA; the recurrence-reduction mechanism is unverified.

claims.text: Best overall accuracy on AuthTrace with the largest gains on high multi-doc queries.
claims.setting: AuthTrace, GPT-4o-mini judge with human audit
claims.result_denominator: judged accuracy; single run; human audit 240 responses on 3 methods
claims.counterevidence: Loses Single-doc to HippoRAG 2; judge slightly permissive (1.6-2.2 points).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Best overall, driven by multi-document columns.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A compiled, linked Wiki traversed by a tool-calling agent substantially outperforms flat-chunk retrieval under the same agent and LLM and outperforms the tested RAG systems at the single-run level on small closed multi-hop corpora; the persistent Error Book plus repair adds a few F1 points in a leave-one-out ablation.
assessment.cannot_claim: That constraint accumulation (rather than deterministic repair) explains the Error Book gain; that errors recur less; large-scale or dynamic-corpus behavior; statistical significance; comparison to agentic iterative RAG.
unresolved: Recurrence of construction errors with vs without constraints.

G.reason: Specific limitation of flat-chunk retrieval and of unchecked LLM-compiled KBs, with named graph/hierarchical RAG neighbors; but persistent LLM-curated agent memories and iterative RAG are not covered as neighbors, and the recurrence premise for the self-evolution part is not evidenced (most errors are mechanically checkable).

M.reason: Compile -> validate -> attribute -> constrain -> inject -> verify/close, with a two-layer code/LLM repair split, gives a reconstructable mechanism that targets named error classes; assumptions about constraint effectiveness and LLM content verification are thinly grounded.

X.reason: Schema, validators, lifecycle (open/closed with periodic re-validation), persistence file, repair cadence and traversal tools are described; but no admission test or cap/conflict handling for constraints, no prompt disclosure, and Wiki versioning/rollback is not described.

E.measurement.reason: Standard F1/EM against gold answers; AuthTrace judge audited by blind annotators (kappa 0.79) with ranking preserved; same corpus and LLM for all methods. Annotators are authors, corpora are small and closed, and closed-book scores are high on public Wikipedia data.

E.causality.reason: Flat-chunk and no-traversal ablations with the same agent are informative, but the Error Book ablation bundles learning with repair, there is no recurrence measurement, no repair-only control, no agentic/iterative RAG baseline, and query-time budgets are unequal; single runs.

E.holdout.reason: The self-evolving loop never sees QA labels or answers, so selection-set leakage is not a concern; but there is no dev/test or construction/evaluation split, hyperparameters (T_max, patience, N) have no stated provenance, the corpora are built from the evaluation questions' own contexts, no cross-corpus transfer of constraints is tested, and parametric memorization is only indirectly visible via closed-book scores.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs on 500 questions per benchmark without seeds, intervals or tests; the smallest claimed gap is 2.0 F1; the only reliability analysis is the judge audit (240 responses).

E.cost.reason: Query latency and pages read are reported for all methods, but index-time compile cost, Error Book/validator overhead and baseline index cost are not quantified; the authors only acknowledge compile cost qualitatively.

rationale: 编译式Wiki+工具遍历显著优于同agent扁平分块;Error Book(验证器驱动约束注入+修复)消融3.4-4.0 F1,但与确定性修复捆绑、无错误复现测量。单次运行、无统计、编译成本未量化。判定retained/scoped。
